paper.title_en: Systematic description of α-induced reactions at intermediate energies within an intranuclear cascade framework
paper.abstract_en: This study validates and generalizes the intermediate-energy α-induced reaction model originally developed in [Phys. Rev. C 112, 024616 (2025)]. We measured double-differential cross sections for five emission channels (<math><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>He</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>3</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and α) using C and Co targets at 230 MeV/u. By optimizing the transition impact parameter <math><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>tr</mi></msub></math> for each target, it was found to be expressed as <math><mrow><mn>1.2</mn><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></math>, where <math><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> is the nuclear radius and <math><mi>a</mi></math> is the diffuseness parameter, reflecting the nuclear-size dependence. The model, employing this universal formulation, successfully reproduced the new experimental data. Furthermore, using the parameters determined from the 230 MeV/u data, the model was tested against existing data at different incident energies up to 800 MeV/u; remarkably, it demonstrated high predictive accuracy without any additional parameter adjustments.
